sn35.133:1.1: On one occasion the Venerable Udāyı̄ was living at Kāmaṇḍā in the brahmin Todeyya’s Mango Grove.
sn35.133:1.2: Then a brahmin youth, a student of the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan, approached the Venerable Udāyı̄ and greeted him.
sn35.133:1.3: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side,
sn35.133:1.4: and the Venerable Udāyı̄ instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him with a Dhamma talk.
sn35.133:1.5: Having been instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened by the Dhamma talk, the brahmin youth rose from his seat, approached the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan, and said to her:
sn35.133:1.6: “See now, madam, you should know that the ascetic Udāyı̄ teaches a Dhamma that is good in the beginning,
sn35.133:1.7: good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals a holy life that is perfectly complete and pure.”
sn35.133:2.1: “In that case, young man, invite the ascetic Udāyı̄ in my name for tomorrow’s meal.”
sn35.133:2.2: “Yes, madam,” the youth replied. Then he went to the Venerable Udāyı̄ and said to him:
sn35.133:2.3: “Let Master Udāyı̄ consent to accept tomorrow’s meal from our revered teacher, the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan.”
sn35.133:2.4: The Venerable Udāyı̄ consented by silence.
sn35.133:2.5: Then, when the night had passed, in the morning the Venerable Udāyı̄ dressed, took his bowl and outer robe, and went to the residence of the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan. There he sat down in the appointed seat.
sn35.133:2.6: Then, with her own hands, the brahmin lady served and satisfied the Venerable Udāyı̄ with various kinds of delicious food.
sn35.133:2.7: When the Venerable Udāyı̄ had finished eating and had put away his bowl, the brahmin lady put on her sandals, sat down on a high seat, covered her head, and told him:
sn35.133:2.9: Having said, “There will be an occasion for that, sister,” he rose from his seat and departed.

sn35.133:3.5: “See now, madam, you should know that the ascetic Udāyı̄ teaches a Dhamma that is good in the beginning,
sn35.133:3.6: good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals a holy life that is perfectly complete and pure.”
sn35.133:4.1: “In such a way, young man, you keep on praising the ascetic Udāyı̄, but when I told him,
sn35.133:4.2: ‘Preach the Dhamma, ascetic,’ he said, ‘There will be an occasion for that, sister,’ and he rose from his seat and departed.”
sn35.133:4.3: “That, madam, was because you put on your sandals, sat down on a high seat, covered your head, and told him:
sn35.133:4.5: For these worthies respect and revere the Dhamma.”
sn35.133:4.6: “In that case, young man, invite the ascetic Udāyı̄ in my name for tomorrow’s meal.”
sn35.133:4.7: “Yes, madam,” he replied. Then he went to the Venerable Udāyı̄ … (all as above ) …
sn35.133:5.3: When the Venerable Udāyı̄ had finished eating and had put away his bowl, the brahmin lady removed her sandals, sat down on a low seat, uncovered her head, and said to him:
sn35.133:5.4: “Venerable sir, what do the arahants maintain must exist for there to be pleasure and pain? And what is it that the arahants maintain must cease to exist for there to be no pleasure and pain?”
sn35.133:6.1: “Sister, the arahants maintain that when the eye exists there is pleasure and pain, and when the eye does not exist there is no pleasure and pain. The arahants maintain that when the ear exists there is pleasure and pain, and when the ear does not exist there is no pleasure and pain….
sn35.133:6.3: The arahants maintain that when the mind exists there is pleasure and pain, and when the mind does not exist there is no pleasure and pain.”
sn35.133:7.1: When this was said, the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan said to the Venerable Udāyı̄:
sn35.133:7.2: “Magnificent, venerable sir! Magnificent, venerable sir! The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Udāyı̄ … (as in §127) . …
sn35.133:7.5: From today let Master Udāyı̄ remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
